sources.title: Empirical Processes: Theory and Applications
sources.author: David Pollard
sources.edition: 1990; NSF-CBMS Regional Conference Series in Probability and Statistics, Volume 2
sources.institution: Yale University; published by the Institute of Mathematical Statistics and the American Statistical Association
sources.legal_access: Complete author-hosted PDF of the IMS/ASA volume, linked from Pollard's Yale page; public download, no access control bypassed.

actual_reading.anchors: Complete contiguous theory portion: introduction and §§1-10. Read definitions, examples, hypotheses and proof context for symmetrization; Rademacher chaining; packing/VC entropy; contraction; manageability; uniform laws; outer convergence; stochastic equicontinuity and functional CLTs. Applications in §§11-14 (PDF pp.65-91, printed pp.57-83), front/back matter and references were not read as focused mathematics.

theorem_hypotheses_and_proof_routes: §2, Theorem 2.2: for independent indexed-process sums and convex increasing Phi, compare the supremum functional to an independent-copy/Rademacher-signed sum. Proof uses Jensen, independent copies and symmetry; preserve the countable/separable or outer-measurability convention.

§3, Lemmas 3.1/3.2/3.4 and Theorem 3.5: Rademacher sub-Gaussian increments, maxima and dyadic chaining on totally bounded pseudometric index sets; the entropy-integral conclusion assumes a suitable continuous/separable version. Equation 3.6 gives the packing-entropy integral form.
§4, Definitions 4.2/4.3, Lemma 4.6 and Theorems 4.7-4.10: pseudodimension/VC growth, Sauer-type combinatorics and polynomial packing bounds, including envelope-weighted function-class conversions.
§5, Theorems 5.1-5.7: stability and contraction; use the source's sign symmetry and centering conventions, including the exact absolute-supremum factor.
§7, Definition 7.9 and maximal inequalities including Theorem 7.10: manageability plus envelope/moment conditions. These are stronger technical hypotheses than a bare finite covering number.

§8, Theorems 8.2-8.3: weak and strong uniform laws for independent arrays under random entropy/manageability and moment assumptions. The weak proof truncates, symmetrizes and reduces to a finite net; retain the random-entropy rate and summability hypotheses.

§9, Definition 9.1 and Representation Theorem 9.4: outer convergence in distribution with a separable Borel limit and measurable approximation errors; this handles process measurability issues that Borel random-element suppliers alone do not address.

§10, Theorem 10.2: finite-dimensional convergence plus stochastic equicontinuity on totally bounded pseudometric T is equivalent to process weak convergence to a tight law on uniformly continuous paths, under the stated separability/outer-convergence framework. Theorem 10.6 gives a functional CLT for independent row-wise arrays under manageability, covariance convergence, bounded second moments, Lindeberg and metric-compatibility conditions.
source_limitations_or_defects: Only the introductory/theory range through §10 was read; the application chapters 11-14 were not read and are not cited as proof support.

The book's measurability conventions include countability, separability and outer probability at different points. A reusable supplier must choose and state one consistent convention rather than quote a theorem name alone.

sources.title: Empirical Processes: Theory and Applications
sources.author: Jon A. Wellner
sources.edition: Special Topics Course, Spring 2005; corrected version June 1, 2005
sources.institution: University of Washington; course notes hosted on the UW faculty site
sources.legal_access: Complete author-hosted university course-notes PDF; public download, no access control bypassed.

actual_reading.anchors: Complete Chapter 1, §§1-10, including proofs, examples and exercises/remarks: empirical measures, weak convergence, maximal inequalities/chaining, Gaussian bounds, symmetrization, GC classes, Donsker classes, VC entropy and approximation entropy; §10 multiplier/bootstrap results were read but are not required as scaffold prerequisites.
Extracted but not read as a focused mathematical unit (Chapter 2). Do not cite it as reviewed.

theorem_hypotheses_and_proof_routes: §2, Proposition 2.1 and Theorem 2.1: tightness/uniformly continuous versions and the finite-dimensional convergence plus asymptotic-equicontinuity criterion in ell-infinity(T).

§3, Theorem 3.1 and Corollaries 3.2/3.4/3.5: chaining and entropy-integral bounds for processes with the stated Orlicz/sub-Gaussian increment assumptions; Lemmas 3.2/3.3 give Bennett/Bernstein inequalities.
§4, Proposition 4.1 and Theorem 4.2: Gaussian concentration and Sudakov lower bound; Gaussian comparison Theorem 4.1 is cited rather than proved.
§5, Lemmas 5.1-5.3: independent-process moment/probability symmetrization by independent copies and Rademacher signs.

§6, Theorems 6.1-6.4: finite L1(P)-bracketing sufficient for GC; the stated necessary/sufficient random L2(P_n)-entropy characterization has measurability and envelope conditions; VC classes give GC under its stated envelope assumptions.

§7, Theorems 7.1/7.4: uniform-entropy and bracketing-entropy integral sufficient conditions for Donsker convergence. Theorem 7.1 uses P-measurability, PF^2<infinity, uniform L2(Q) entropy integrability and measurability of difference/square classes; proof combines symmetrization, sub-Gaussian chaining and local-square GC control. Theorems 7.7/7.8 treat triangular-array CLT and a bounded universal Donsker characterization.

§8, Lemma 8.1 and Theorems 8.1-8.2: Sauer-Shelah growth and uniform Lr covering entropy for VC sets and VC-subgraph function classes, with envelope scaling; examples and convex-hull entropy are also covered.

§9, Theorems 9.1/9.4/9.5: approximation/bracketing entropy examples for smooth and monotone classes, including examples whose entropy exponent prevents a Donsker conclusion. §10 multiplier-process theorems were read but are outside the core pair dependency graph.
source_limitations_or_defects: Theorem 4.1 is a cited Gaussian comparison result, not a proof in this unit; it is not proposed as a theorem supplier here.
The notes use P-measurability and separability assumptions that must be reconciled with Pollard's outer-convergence formulation at authoring time.
Only Chapter 1 was fully read; Chapter 2 was extracted but not reviewed.

sources.title: High-Dimensional Statistics: Lecture Notes
sources.author: Philippe Rigollet and Jan-Christian Hütter
sources.edition: MIT 18.657 lecture notes; cover dated October 29, 2023; arXiv:2310.19244v1 submitted October 30, 2023. The notes report that the material is based on Princeton notes from 2013-14 and 2017 content was uploaded without change.
sources.institution: Massachusetts Institute of Technology; full author-deposited arXiv version
sources.legal_access: Public author-deposited arXiv full text; no access control bypassed.

actual_reading.anchors: Introduction and Chapter 1 concentration unit: sub-Gaussian/sub-exponential variables, Hoeffding lemma/tail, Bernstein, finite maxima, epsilon-net vector bounds and matrix Bernstein. Complete focused chapter read with proofs and examples.

Complete Chapter 2 fixed-design linear regression unit: prediction/fitted-value risk, least squares, constrained l1/l0 procedures, BIC, Lasso, incoherence, cone/restricted-eigenvalue step and Slope. Read proof assumptions and computational/statistical distinctions.
Complete Chapter 3 oracle-inequality and approximation unit, including least squares/BIC/Lasso results, Maurey approximation and Sobolev/trigonometric examples.

Complete Chapter 4 minimax lower-bound unit: risk definitions, packing reduction, Neyman-Pearson/TV/KL/Pinsker, two-point and Fano bounds, Varshamov-Gilbert sparse packings, Assouad-related detection examples and constrained-risk/moment-matching results.
Extracted but not read as a focused mathematical unit (Chapter 5 and following). Do not cite it as reviewed.

theorem_hypotheses_and_proof_routes: Chapter 1, Definition 1.2/Lemma 1.3, Lemma 1.8/Theorem 1.9, Lemmas 1.10/1.12/Theorem 1.13, Theorems 1.14/1.19/1.27: MGF/tail equivalences, Hoeffding, Bernstein, maximum of N possibly dependent sub-Gaussian variables, epsilon-net vector norm and matrix Bernstein.

Chapter 2, Theorem 2.2: fixed-design fitted-value least-squares MSE/high-probability bounds under subG_n(sigma^2) noise; coefficient error needs a minimum-eigenvalue/design condition. Theorem 2.4: unit l1-constrained least squares under theta* in B1 and normalized design columns. Theorem 2.6/Corollaries 2.8-2.9: k-sparse constrained least squares via a union over supports; it needs no design compatibility but is combinatorial. Theorem 2.14: BIC-type sparse oracle bound without design assumptions. Theorem 2.15: Lasso slow rate. Assumption INC(k), Proposition 2.16, Lemma 2.17 and Theorem 2.18: random Rademacher designs can satisfy incoherence; cone plus compatibility gives fast Lasso fitted-value/coefficient rates under the theorem's column normalization and sparsity assumptions. Theorem 2.22 is a Slope bound under a stronger incoherence condition.

Chapter 3, Theorems 3.3-3.7 and Theorem 3.15/Corollary 3.16: least-squares/BIC/Lasso oracle inequalities, Maurey sparse approximation, and nonparametric risk examples. These are read in full proof context but only the oracle results are proposed for reuse.

Chapter 4, Definitions 4.1-4.2 and §4.2: minimax risk and nearest-packing reduction. Lemma 4.3/Proposition 4.4 and Proposition 4.6/Lemma 4.8: testing, TV, KL product additivity and the stated weaker Pinsker bound TV<=sqrt(KL). Theorems 4.9-4.11, Lemma 4.12 and Corollaries 4.13-4.16: two-point/Fano/packing and dense/sparse Gaussian-sequence rates. Later Chapter 4 sections include a chi-square sparse-detection lower bound and a constrained-risk inequality; these are not needed for the core scaffold.
source_limitations_or_defects: Theorem 2.2 controls fitted-value error; coefficient error requires full-rank conditioning or an explicit compatibility condition. Do not exchange these losses silently.
Theorem 2.6's constrained l0 estimator searches over supports and is an information-theoretic benchmark, not a polynomial-time guarantee.

The fast Lasso theorem requires the notes' incoherence/RE hypotheses and column normalization; a generic design matrix does not inherit the rate. The theorem's confidence tuning must remain in its statement.
The read Slope result uses Gaussian noise and stronger compatibility assumptions; it is not needed to claim the sparse constrained-LS minimax match.
Only the introduction and Chapters 1-4 were read; later chapters were not.

sources.title: Lecture Notes on Statistics and Information Theory
sources.author: John Duchi
sources.edition: PDF dated December 6, 2023; Statistics 311 / Electrical Engineering 377 author notes; Stanford course site was checked for institutional/course authority.
sources.legal_access: Public Stanford-hosted course notes; public download, no access control bypassed.

actual_reading.anchors: Complete focused Chapter 8 §§8.1-8.5: minimax risk/excess risk, packing reduction, total variation/KL/Hellinger and Pinsker relations, Le Cam, Fano (including local and distance-based forms), and Assouad with examples. Proofs and examples were read.
Chapter 8 §8.7 global Fano and its KL-covering application.
Not read as focused mathematics. In particular §8.6 applications and §8.8 deferred proofs were skipped; no claim of full-book reading is made.

theorem_hypotheses_and_proof_routes: §8.1.1/8.1.3: minimax risk and excess risk definitions, with expectations and probability-law indexing made explicit.
§8.2.1 Proposition 8.2.1: estimation-to-testing reduction from a metric packing. §8.2.2 gives TV/KL/Hellinger/Pinsker comparisons, product KL additivity and Hellinger product behavior.
§8.3 Le Cam, equations 8.3.1-8.3.3, plus Bernoulli-mean example: nearest-point testing and total-variation lower bound.
§8.4 Proposition 8.4.1/Corollary 8.4.2: Fano and error lower bounds; local Fano uses average KL; Propositions 8.4.6 and Corollaries 8.4.7-8.4.8 give distance-based forms and examples.
§8.5 Lemma 8.5.2: Assouad hypercube lower bound through neighboring-coordinate TV distances; Gaussian-mean and logistic examples. State the loss/coordinate metric conversion separately.

§8.7 Proposition 8.7.1/Corollary 8.7.2: global Fano via mutual information bounded by a KL covering functional; the iid form exposes the n-fold divergence factor. The nonparametric regression example is within the read range.
source_limitations_or_defects: Only the specified Chapter 8 sections were read, not all 495 PDF pages.
The notes present several alternative TV/Pinsker normalizations; a new theorem must fix one convention and check constants in the translated risk bound.
Section 8.8 deferred proofs were not read. The scaffold uses the proved Chapter 8 units rather than citing a deferred proof as if it were present.

sources.title: Probability tools, tricks, and miracles
sources.author: David Pollard
sources.edition: Author manuscript, version 22 June 2026; unpublished manuscript hosted on Pollard's Yale page.
sources.legal_access: Public author-hosted complete manuscript PDF; no access control bypassed. Treated as an unpublished author manuscript, not as a published text or as carrying an open-license claim.

actual_reading.anchors: Complete Chapter 10 on chaining: maximal inequalities, Brownian-motion dyadic example, finite chaining frameworks, total boundedness and covering/packing relations, Orlicz maxima, packing entropy integrals, and oscillation/continuity result.

Complete Chapter 11 on majorizing measures and partitions, §§11.1-11.12: mm definition, nested/non-nested partitions, mm construction intuition, smoothing proof, weighted-framework maximal bound, admissible partitions, comparison example where packing entropy fails, problems, notes and references.

Complete Chapter 12 on Gaussian majorizing measures, §§12.1-12.7: strengthened Sudakov lemma, recursive weighted partitions, necessity for bounded/uniformly continuous Gaussian paths, admissible-partition construction, proof caveat, problems, notes and references.

Complete Chapter 13 on symmetrization, §§13.1-13.8: independent-copy product-space method, empirical-process motivation, convex-function moment symmetrization, tail symmetrization, square-root trick and oscillation argument, examples/problems/notes/references.

Complete Chapter 14 on VC sets, §§14.1-14.7: probabilistic trace/packing argument, VC and shatter dimension, Sauer bound by downshift, graph edge count, Haussler packing bound, problems, notes and references.
Not read as focused mathematics. Other concentration, measurability and process chapters were not cited as reviewed.

theorem_hypotheses_and_proof_routes: §10.6: for sub-Gaussian/Orlicz increments on a totally bounded pseudometric index set, telescope through finite nets and sum scale-wise maxima; the entropy integral controls expected/Orlicz suprema under the chapter's separability assumptions. §10.7 adds an oscillation/tightness conclusion under a finite approximation property.

§11.5, Theorem 21: a doob-separable process with increments controlled by an Orlicz norm in Yexp and weighted chaining-framework links has a maximal inequality whose bound separates path-specific weighted entropy terms from a summable remainder. §11.7 gives an admissible-partition upper bound. §11.9 exhibits a bounded Gaussian supremum where the ordinary packing integral diverges but majorizing-measure/weighted/admissible methods succeed.

§12.1, Lemma 2 and §§12.2/12.4: centered countable/separable Gaussian processes with canonical increment metric; Sudakov minoration plus recursive greedy partitions yields necessity-style lower bounds for weighted/admissible partition functionals. The author explicitly cautions in §12.4 that the assembled proof may contain errors; do not use this alone as the proof source for a gated generic-chaining theorem.

§13.2, Theorems 12-13: countable-index independent processes; Jensen/Fubini on product spaces gives convex-function symmetrization, while a first-index witness and an independent-copy small-event condition give probability inequalities. §§13.4-13.6 derive Rademacher maximal and oscillation bounds, with envelope, variance, packing and truncation conditions stated locally.

§14.2, Theorem 4 and §14.3, Theorem 9: VC/shatter dimension gives polynomial trace growth by a finite downshift argument that preserves shattered row sets. §14.2 Example 14 and §14.5 Theorem 23: random projection and a conditional-variance graph argument yield uniform weighted-Hamming packing bounds for VC classes.
source_limitations_or_defects: This is an unpublished author manuscript and only Chapters 10-14 were read; complete extraction must not be described as complete mathematical reading.

The author explicitly says in §12.4 that he would be pleasantly surprised if the assembled admissible-partition proof were error-free. Treat its Gaussian generic-chaining necessity result as corroboration/motivation pending an independent complete proof, not as the sole support for a theorem supplier.
The generic Orlicz/partition arguments impose doob-separability, Yexp growth, totally boundedness and link/weight constraints. They do not justify dropping measurability or increment hypotheses.

reading_summary: The full PDFs were extracted. The complete Pollard 1990 theory part through §10, complete Wellner 2005 Chapter 1, complete Rigollet-Hütter Chapters 1-4, selected complete Duchi Chapter 8 sections, and complete Pollard 2026 Chapters 10-14 were read. Exact PDF and printed-page boundaries and the un-read portions are recorded source by source. Independent full-text treatments corroborate the core symmetrization/entropy/GC/Donsker/minimax routes; no second complete generic Gaussian majorizing-measure proof was read.
